label: Metric Views, Pages, Domains and governing layer
teaching_intent: Build a concrete hierarchy of curated semantic objects rather than decorative graph nodes.
original_transcript: definition for your key business metrics stored as open format Unity Catalog objects. So, for example, you know, this is how we slice and dice revenue. And and metric views are fully GA'd. Pages are a bit newer. Uh it's the it's the qualitative equivalent of a metric view. I think of them as wiki pages in in Unity Catalog. So, if a metric view defines how we slice and dice revenue, a page might tell you, say, the difference between incremental and attributed revenue. Uh and these are in beta and it is actually super easy to get started. You can use Genie code to actually get started on creating your pages. And then finally, domains uh allow you to do tag-based logical collections of assets, uh both Unity Catalog and workspace assets by things like business unit or geo or function. So, you might have a finance domain or you might have a product team domain. And an asset can live in multiple domains. And it's really helpful for reducing the agent's search space. So, if someone asks a question about finance, you know, we can start from from the finance domain. So, together, metric views, pages, and domains form this certified authoritative baseline. But it's hard, if not impossible, to try to codify the entire organization's knowledge that way, to have a centralized data team responsible for codifying the the concepts that every individual team are are kind of experts in. So, we supplement the modeled ontology
